gap: None of ChatGPT's results say that ResMed's own AirSense 11 DC/DC converter (ref 39231) switches itself off when its supply is too low to run the machine (its light turns amber first), or that ResMed recommends a deep-cycle battery as the source. Nor do they say the converter sells in the US for $95 with no prescription.
standout_why: Compared against willitrunpower.com/best-power-station-for/cpap (cited) and preparedstates.com/guides/power-station-for-cpap (cited); amphourly, juicebench and the Reddit thread were not opened. willitrunpower already has the converter's 12 V/24 V, 10 A/5 A input and 24 V, 3.75 A output, notes that a 10 A car port matches, and says ResMed's converter runs the HumidAir humidifier and ClimateLineAir heated tube. preparedstates gives no converter specs. Neither page has the converter's low-battery shutoff, ResMed's deep-cycle battery recommendation, the US price, or the no-prescription status. So only part of my finding is new, and it doesn't change the pick on its own.
decides: It supports the BLUETTI AC180 pick and doesn't change it. BLUETTI's AC180 page lists a regulated 12V/10A car outlet, which matches the 10 A at 12 V input on ResMed's converter page. The converter switches off when its supply runs too low, so you should test a full night at home before the trip. The page should list the converter (ResMed ref 39231, $95, no prescription per cpapsupplies.com) as a required add-on to the AC180, about $594 in total at today's $499 BLUETTI price.

findings.label: Input and output rating
findings.value: Input 12 V / 24 V at 10 A / 5 A; output 24 V at 3.75 A; 3 m lead; 12-month warranty; 5-year design life
findings.note: This is ResMed's own store page, for UK sale only. I couldn't open a ResMed US page for this part. The output works out to 24 × 3.75 = 90 W.

findings.label: Humidifier and heated tube on DC
findings.value: ResMed's page says it powers an AirSense 11 with the HumidAir humidifier and ClimateLineAir heated tube
findings.note: This is a maker statement. willitrunpower already reports it.

findings.label: Low-battery behaviour and recommended source
findings.value: Indicator is green when on and amber when the vehicle battery is low. When the battery is too low to run the device, the converter and its light turn off. ResMed recommends a deep-cycle battery and says to unplug the converter when not in use.
findings.note: Paraphrased from the maker page, which gives no cutoff voltage. The included user guide isn't linked in a form I could open.

findings.label: US price, prescription status
findings.value: $95.00, in stock, no prescription required, FSA/HSA eligible
findings.source_title: Resmed AirSense 11 AutoSet Auto-CPAP Machine DC-DC Power Converter | CPAPsupplies.com
findings.note: US retailer page listing model 39231 and UPC 619498392315. It says the converter powers 'both the AirSense 11 Auto-CPAP Machine and the Humidifier'.

findings.label: 12 V car outlet
findings.note: The rating equals the converter's 10 A input at 12 V. The page mentions an ECO mode that turns outputs on and off automatically, but gives no thresholds and doesn't say whether it covers the DC outlet.
